assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine formation, previously a painful problem, into a routine, general transformation. Ligand design (bulky, electron-rich phosphines) made the reaction broad in scope, and it is used daily in medicinal chemistry, process chemistry and materials synthesis. New chemistry, simple concept, vast adoption: the profile of a method prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, general versions and the ligand families that made it practical. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling (and Migita's related work, if I recall correctly) is a precursor but not the decisive step, so a two-person prize looks defensible.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty-five years of independent use, including large-scale pharmaceutical manufacture. Fully mature; if anything recognition is late. Close in kind to the 2010 cross-coupling prize, which could be read as either a precedent or a reason for delay.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as too close to the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize.
Relative weight of Kosugi's precursor work; I have not verified the exact priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and excited-state pathways to mild bond constructions and is now routinely used in discovery chemistry and increasingly in process settings. It changed how synthetic chemists think about single-electron steps and enables dual catalysis with Ni and others. Strong evidence of broad uptake in countless syntheses.
assessment.attribution: The 2008-2009 work of MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson is usually seen as the starting point of the modern synthetic field. The credit is spread among many (Konig, Nicewicz, Melchiorre, Fukuzumi), so any trio is contestable. MacMillan already holds a prize (2021, organocatalysis), which may bias the committee against including him.
assessment.maturity: Roughly 15 years old with huge, independent uptake. Mechanistic details are still being refined in places, but the practical impact is firmly established.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would accept a prior laureate in a new trio.
Crowded credit and possible allocation disputes among at least seven names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalyst-controlled C-H functionalization changes retrosynthetic logic by allowing the use of ubiquitous C-H bonds as handles, which is the efficiency argument I care most about. Directing-group and ligand-enabled Pd chemistry (Yu) and Pd(II/IV) and related oxidative chemistry (Sanford) now appear in late-stage functionalization and total synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Yu's ligand-accelerated, template-controlled meta/remote and enantioselective C-H activation is the most general advance; Sanford's mechanistic and methodological work is also decisive. Hartwig's borylation work is relevant but he overlaps with B031, and Daugulis and Smith are also credited, so the boundary is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Younger than C-N coupling, and routine industrial use is still growing but not yet universal. Selectivity and scope limits remain, so there is a case for waiting a few more years.
uncertainties: Industrial uptake still moderate compared with cross-coupling.
Disputed boundaries with Bergman-era alkane activation (B035) and with Hartwig's borylation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides and made total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins practical. It is a clear case of a chemical concept (thioester exchange followed by S-to-N acyl shift) with wide use in protein science, including modified proteins and therapeutic leads.
assessment.attribution: Dawson, Muir and Kent introduced NCL in 1994 (Dawson, Muir, Clark-Lewis, Kent), and Muir pioneered expressed protein ligation. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu extended it, so the trio is defensible, but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of confirmed use. Mature, with limitations in scale and cost keeping it a research tool more than a manufacturing platform.
uncertainties: Biology-adjacent: some colleagues will ask how much is new chemistry beyond Merrifield-type synthesis.
Priority and credit interplay with Danishefsky and Liu.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry is the basis of nearly all synthetic DNA and RNA and underlies PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide drugs. As a chemist I find it a compelling case of a robust, high-yielding, automatable coupling cycle that enabled a whole field.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method (Beaucage and Caruthers, 1981). Hood is credited for the automated instrumentation, which is engineering rather than the core chemical invention; I would give the prize to Caruthers alone, though a second name might be argued.
assessment.maturity: Over forty years of universal use; fully mature, and perhaps overdue. The risk is that its time has passed, and Nobel precedent for nucleic acid synthesis (Khorana, Smith) may be seen as covering some ground.
uncertainties: Whether Hood's contribution is chemical or instrumental; my reading of the supplied credit is that it is instrumental.
Possible overlap with earlier prizes in nucleic acid chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically encumbered acid-base pairs can heterolytically cleave H2 and activate other small molecules without metals. It is a conceptually simple and original idea that broadened main-group reactivity and led to metal-free hydrogenation.
assessment.attribution: Stephan reported the first metal-free reversible H2 activation (2006) and Erker developed related systems and catalysis; two people fit well.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many labs, but practical impact, particularly industrial, is limited so far. Prize timing could be premature relative to application.
uncertainties: Whether the conceptual novelty is enough without major catalytic use.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolable stable carbenes (imidazolylidenes, and Bertrand's cyclic alkyl amino and phosphino carbenes) changed ligand design and organocatalysis; NHC ligands underpin the modern metathesis and cross-coupling catalysts that I use as a synthetic chemist.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand's 1988 phosphinocarbene and Arduengo's 1991 crystalline NHC are the key discoveries. Nolan, Bode and Rovis are credited for the follow-on application, so two names are the cleaner core.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of use. Fully mature, though impact is mostly as an enabling ligand class, which could make it feel supporting rather than primary.
uncertainties: Ligand-class impact is distributed across many other prize-recognized reactions.
Relative priority of Bertrand's earlier carbene versus Arduengo's isolable NHC.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: ATRP gave controlled radical polymerization of many monomers with defined architectures and low dispersity using simple metal catalysis. It is widely used in materials and industry, but it sits slightly outside my own field of small-molecule synthesis, so I rank it below the synthetic methodology candidates.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto independently reported the metal-catalyzed process in 1995; Wang, Kamigaito and others are credited, but two would be the most natural pair.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use and mature. Competing methods, particularly RAFT (B061), share the same field, so a fair allocation could be difficult.
uncertainties: Overlap with RAFT and nitroxide-mediated polymerization if the committee wants to recognize controlled radical polymerization as a whole.
Parallel priority between Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto.
